title: FLIIMP - Community Software for Liquid Water Isotope Measurements
author: Sodemann, Mørkved, et al.
materials: Step 5 in the FLIIMP processing sequence is the specification of the information needed for producing the report, and for performing the calibration (or normalisation) to VSMOW-SLAP scale. First, the instrument drift during the run can be quantified and assessed. Furthermore, inspection of control standards allows to judge the performance of the measurement system during a given run. Finally, the processing report is exported, containing all information for internal monitoring or for an end user.

steps.title: Start FLIIMP and load files
steps.instruction: Launch FLIIMP in interactive mode by running FLIIMP.m in MATLAB or opening the compiled app icon; in the first panel enter the input and output folder paths, select the instrument, and specify the analysis time range (start date required, end date optional) using the format YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS (or a partial pattern such as 20220501_01*). If the run consists of a single output file omit the end date. For non‑matching file names, click “Select files” to add files manually. Test the setup with the example data file provided in the repository.

steps.title: Screen samples and select pre‑processing
steps.instruction: After confirming the file list, FLIIMP loads and combines all files that match the instrument and time pattern and displays them in the sample‑screening window. Use this window to: (1) identify and flag sample or injection outliers, (2) optionally apply mixing‑ratio‑dependent baseline correction, and (3) assign quality flags to each sample. Memory correction can be enabled later in Step 3.

substeps.instruction: Load and combine files matching the specified pattern.
Inspect data and flag outliers.
Apply baseline correction if needed.
Assign quality flags to each sample.

steps.title: Perform memory correction
steps.instruction: Open the Memory correction panel via the “Memory correction” button. The correction uses a two‑component exponential model Mj = C0 [ w e^(‑a j) + (1‑w) e^(‑b j) ] where w∈[0…1] and a, b are the fast and slow decay exponents. Follow these substeps:

substeps.instruction: Determine memory‑correction coefficients using calibration or drift standards that have at least 10 injections (example: standards with 10 injections, samples with 6 injections – only standards are used for coefficient fitting).
Calculate the final raw δ‑value ỹi for each sample i by averaging the last n of N injections: ỹi = ⟨yN‑ni,…,yNi⟩.
Compute the percent memory Mji affecting sample i at injection j: Mji = (ỹi‑ỹi‑1) / (ỹi‑ỹi‑1) × 100 % (negative values are retained).
Weight each memory estimate by βi = |ỹi‑1‑ỹi| / Σ|ỹk‑1‑ỹk| to give more influence to large inter‑sample δ differences.
Fit the model (Eq. 3) to the weighted estimates Mji·βi by minimizing root‑mean‑square error (RMSE).
Force the fitted correction M̃ji to zero for the last n injections using linear deprecation: M̂ji = M̃ji – M̃N‑1i · [1‑(N‑j)/N].
Apply the final correction M̂ji to all samples; the routine FLIIMP_memory_analysis.m performs this computation.

steps.title: Edit sample names and IDs
steps.instruction: In the Sample renaming panel, modify sample names and identifiers as needed: click a row in the left table to edit fields in the top‑right pane, or use the lower‑right controls to (a) swap all sample names with their IDs, (b) assign new IDs based on a user‑provided base string plus a sequential number starting at the specified Start index, while skipping any names listed in the Standards field (space‑separated). Modified entries appear in orange and can be restored at any time.

substeps.instruction: Edit individual sample name or ID by selecting the row and typing in the edit fields.
Swap all names and IDs with the “Swap” button if they were entered incorrectly.
Assign new IDs: provide a base string and a Start index; the software appends sequential numbers.
Enter standard sample names in the Standards field to exclude them from renaming.
Restore original names/IDs if needed.

steps.title: Specify calibration and export report
steps.instruction: In the final panel, set all calibration and reporting parameters: choose the calibration set, list calibration standards (space‑separated), and designate drift and control standards. Activate or deactivate pre‑processing options (humidity‑dependency correction, drift correction, memory correction). To limit processing to the last n injections, enter a positive integer; entering –1 uses all available injections. Provide a project name and a run identifier, then click the “Calibrate” button. FLIIMP creates a new output folder containing calibrated data files and a full processing report for internal monitoring or end‑user delivery.

substeps.instruction: Select calibration set and list calibration standard names.
Specify drift and control standards.
Toggle pre‑processing steps (humidity, drift, memory).
Enter n (or –1 for all injections) to define how many injections are used.
Enter project name and run identifier.
Click Calibrate to generate output files and the processing report.
